newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export prices seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export prices seen stable.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices that remained unchanged in the domestic market due to low demand from the Gulf are expected to remain stable next week, dealers said on Thursday.

One official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan said the Corporation had invited bids by May 26 for the sale and export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 rice containing seven percent broken.
Bids could also be submitted for two lots of 2,500 tonnes each, the official said.
The dealer said Monday's auction would indicate future export prices of basmati rice.

Pakistan exported 1.571 million tonnes of rice worth $393 million in the first 10 months to April of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) compared to 1.133 million tonnes worth $372 million in the same period a year ago.
In April, rice exports fell to 180,094 tonnes worth $48 million compared to 372,828 tonnes worth $62 million in March and 118,141 tonnes worth $38 million in April 1996.
